incident_description: Russian guided aerial bombs struck a former school in Komyshuvakha used as a humanitarian aid distribution point and shelter. A second strike hit the shelter after emergency services arrived. The final confirmed toll after a two-week search-and-rescue operation was 72 deaths. The victims included civilians, police officers, rescuers, school and administrative-services-centre staff, municipal workers and medical personnel. Four people remained missing at the conclusion of the operation and are excluded.

revision_history.reason: Initial regional administration update reported one person killed in the attack.
Later Nov. 2 regional administration update raised the incident toll to 18.
The State Emergency Service reported 24 deaths later on Nov. 2, including two rescuers and four police officers.
The Nov. 3 morning update raised the incident toll from 24 to 29. The earlier Nov. 2 DSNS update had reported 24.
Acting regional administration head Mykhailo Semikin reported 31 deaths at 11:40. This was a new higher incident count, not an additional 31 deaths.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported 33 deaths later on Nov. 3. This interim update is retained even though subsequent recoveries raised the count further.
Acting regional administration head Mykhailo Semikin reported 37 deaths on Nov. 4.
Later Nov. 4 update raised the toll to 40. This is the revised incident total, not a second addition of 40.
National Police reported 42 bodies recovered on the fourth day of search operations.

The president confirmed one further death, bringing the incident toll to 43. A separate pair of police officers who died in hospital from a Nov. 1 attack near Komyshuvakha are not included in this incident record.
DSNS reported 50 deaths at 10:49 after recovering eight additional bodies.
Semikin's 10:51 update raised the toll from the DSNS figure of 50 at 10:49 to 53. These are sequential updates, not numbers to be added together.
DSNS reported the toll had risen to 55. The regional administration confirmed 55 recovered bodies on Nov. 8.

The search-and-rescue operation concluded after two weeks. The final confirmed toll was 72, including non-combatant emergency personnel and municipal/public-service workers. Four people remained missing and are not counted.
